name: Manahath
overview: Manahath was a male Edomite, identified in Scripture as the son of Shobal. His mention is brief and specific, with no additional notes expanding on his life or deeds. He is part of the genealogical record of the Edomites, a people descended from Esau.
namesAndTitles: The name Manahath means 'resting place' in Hebrew. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a peaceful connotation consistent with Hebrew naming practices. The name appears specifically in Genesis 36:23.
familyAndRelationships: Manahath is explicitly identified as the son of Shobal in Genesis 36:23. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections or descendants for Manahath.
scriptureSignificance: Manahath's significance lies primarily in his role within the Edomite genealogy, serving as a link in the lineage recorded in Genesis 36. His mention helps establish the historical and tribal context of the Edomites, who are important in biblical history as descendants of Esau. Though not a central figure in the narrative, Manahath's inclusion underscores the biblical emphasis on heritage and divine providence in the unfolding story of God's people.
